title: Prognostic prediction of pulmonary neuroendocrine carcinoma using a transformer-based artificial intelligence model: a two-center retrospective cohort study.
summary: A two-center retrospective cohort compared a transformer-based model with conventional approaches for overall and disease-free survival prediction. The best-performing model differed by endpoint, so performance should be described by task rather than as one universal winner.
organization: Peking Union Medical College Hospital; Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences

evidence.tested: Two-center retrospective cohort evaluation reported model-specific discrimination for overall and disease-free survival.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective cohorts do not establish prospective clinical benefit; the strongest model varied by endpoint.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
